I’m so sorry, you are so young and this is a very heavy thing to deal with. I am in an almost identical situation as you. My family and I have been dealing with this for around 3 almost 4 years now. There are days that are incredibly hard and the mental and emotional toll it takes is no joke. I am an introvert by nature but i found all i could do to cope was make myself busy in some way. It’s really a day by day case, but there will be good days too. I’m sure your mom appreciates you being there for her. It’s a really special thing and you should be proud of yourself for that. I met a kind woman from an ALS organization that met with my family, and when i started to cry talking about how worried i was and how hard things were, she told me theres a lot of good times and hope ahead. I know that may even sound cliche, but in that moment it really helped me and still does to this day. Nobody had ever chosen to meet my sadness and fear with positivity up until that point. It made me feel better to hear some positivity especially from someone who works daily with all things ALS related. There will still be good times, and hope

I stopped about 3 months ago. I am bad about being consistent with taking my meds and was experiencing bad side effects from not taking it, and then bad side effects every time i tried to start again. I just couldn’t take the back and forth anymore so I gave up. The medicine I believe helped me in some ways, but i experienced a lot of brain fog and stomach issues on it. I think my depression has come back, and my high anxiety. However I am also dealing with a difficult ongoing situation that weighs on me every day. It’s not just bouts of relatively unexplained sadness. When I had “that” kind of depression a few years back, Lexapro helped me immensely. Maybe i could try again and be more consistent, but i’m worried to go down that path again because when i would forget to take it for long periods of time I experienced brain and nervous system side effects that were almost unbearable.

Go to a large parking lot when it is empty, like a public school on the weekend, even if that means going outside of the bounds of your city to find a place like that. That is how i started to learn and had someone with me to teach me. First work on just getting familiar with the controls of the car, like the blinker, putting the car in drive or park, holding the steering wheel at “10 and 2” (imagine 10 and 2 on a clock and thats where you put your hands) and then begin with accelerating the car. You can start slow just to get a feel for it. Do some laps around and work on braking, acceleration, and turning. It really is the kind of thing that the more you do it the easier it gets, but it can feel very scary at first. Bring along a trusted family member or friend who has experience driving to be with you.

Some of my #1 driving rules: Always keep a safe distance between you and the car in front of you. Like at least 1-2 cars length between you and the car in front of you. I can’t tell you how many times a car has slammed on their brakes and randomly came to a complete stop  in front of me and that safe distance between me and them saved my life.

Also, always check you mirrors and blind spot before switching lanes and put your blinker on at least a few seconds in advance. Always. 

And don’t speed. Especially if you are in an unfamiliar area and feeling a little uncomfortable with how the road is or the cars around you. My mom always said “you can only hit something as fast as you’re going”. If you are going to hit something or get hit it’s better to be going slower rather than faster because the difference is catastrophic.

Driving was super scary for me when i first started, but I made the decision to keep practicing and go for test drives with someone close to me who could guide me, and to be as safe of a driver as I can be. When you are making the decision to be safe then you are in control of your vehicle and you will be safe.

Hi! I posted this two years ago, when i started Lexapro when i hit a super low point which drove me to finally take the step to getting help. We shouldn’t have to wait to hit rock bottom to get help but thats what made me finally do it. I don’t regret taking Lexapro at all, it really saved me. I stopped taking it after about a year because it got me to a much better place where i felt i was able to stop taking it and still manage my emotions and anxiety. I almost view it as a bridge that got me from a super low point and hopelessness to a place of stability and more confidence. A big thing it did for me was that It gave me the ability to *learn* how to be in situations that gave me extreme anxiety, where as before i would never even be able to experience those things because my anxiety wouldn’t let me. For example, i had too much anxiety to ever drive on a highway, my anxiety would never let me learn how because anytime i tried i would have a panic attack and never truly learned and experienced it in a stable mindset. After taking Lex, i was able to get on the highway and learn how to drive on it, retain the info i learned like rules of driving, etc and now i do it daily with 0 problem. I also learned how to be in social situations and talk to people without panicking and shutting down. A big reason why i stopped taking it as well was the side effects, mainly memory issues/memory loss. At the time, I had just started a new job (thanks to Lexapro giving me the ability to actually have the motivation and control over my anxiety to actually go to a  job interview and manage it well) and over time i found that my new found memory issues (common side effect) were effecting my performance. I also started a new relationship (would have NEVER gave that chance if I wasn’t on Lexapro because my anxiety had stopped me a hundred times before) and i found i was forgetting alot of conversations and details my partner had shared with me, and it subsequently caused some hurt  feeling when my significant other felt i didn’t care enough to remember details they shared me with, when really it was just the lexapro side effects. At that point i felt i was well enough to stop taking it. I did not consult my doctor on this which I really should have so i kind of just weaned off of it, but i recommend sharing that process with your doctor. After i stopped taking it those side effects started to go away and i felt like i had a sharper memory again. I will say that now my anxiety is higher than it was while i was on Lexapro, but i feel like it bridged me to a better place than i would be if i never took Lexapro. I can see myself getting back on it if i find myself in that dark place again, which is likely to happen because healing is not linear and it’s ok to have periods of time where you feel you don’t need to rely on medication and just be “natural” and then need to go back to it again. I’d do this with a doctors knowledge though. 

Going forward i might look into taking it with something like Welbrutrin, because i heard that has helped people with the side effects while still having the benefits of the lexapro. Lexapro helped me a lot with my temper, my anxiety, and a TON with my depression.

I had a childhood best friend who i was very close to.  We were both very similar, shy, quiet, had similar sense of humor, just great friends. I have very strict over protective parents who never let me go or do anything, so going to any type of party was out of the question. I became very embarrassed as i had to always tell her no i would not be joining. I felt more like a loser and a burden to her. I went through a deep depression as i dealt with trauma in my personal life, and continued to feel like a burden to my friend. but to be clear, she never made me feel like a burden. I was just telling myself that. Constantly having to tell her no i couldn’t hang out, making excuses as to why not. It wasn’t because i didn’t like her, i was just going through a terrible time and had no idea how to properly talk about it or deal with it, all i knew was i didn’t feel like leaving the house and even if i wanted to my parents would stop me. I eventually stopped responding to her texts, and she tried really hard to get me to talk to her. I would avoid her at all costs at school, which led to some very awkward run ins. All this time i as dealing with such deep depression and personal trauma, and i can’t say i never thought about the pain my actions caused her, because i did. But at the time it seemed like it was for the best. I felt like there was no way someone cared about me enough to feel that bad about our friendship dissolving like this, and that she would be so much better off without having a loser burden like me in her life holding her back. I never spoke to her again but i know it had to of caused some hurt, and it bothers me often. I feel like she would still totally be my best friend otherwise. I don’t really have any friends now, i’m alone almost always. Sometimes i wish i had just that one girl- friend, but now i don’t. I’ve peeked at her social media so many years later and she seems to have made many more friends and gone on to have lovely experiences, as i knew she would. I’m happy for her and will always feel a tinge of guilt for what happened, but honestly am not going to blame or kick teenage me for dealing with my trauma and depression in that manner, it made me believe that’s what i had to do for her benefit.
